claim: The minimal area of an isospectral-nonisometric pair of 2-orbifolds associated to maximal arithmetic Fuchsian groups is 23*pi/6, achieved by exactly three pairs up to isomorphism, all with orbifold signature (0; 2,2,2,2,2,3,4).
stance_target: existence of genuine published isospectral non-isometric hyperbolic 2-orbifold pairs
scope_conditions: hyperbolic 2-orbifolds X(Gamma) for Gamma a maximal arithmetic Fuchsian group
quoted_support: Theorem A. The minimal area of an isospectral-nonisometric pair of 2-orbifolds associated to maximal arithmetic Fuchsian groups is 23π/6, and this bound is achieved by exactly three pairs, up to isomorphism.

claim: The three minimal-area isospectral pairs are hyperbolic 2-orbifolds with 7 cone points (five order-2, one order-3, one order-4), not triangle orbifolds (which have exactly 3 cone points), so this construction does not bear on the existence of isospectral hyperbolic TRIANGLE orbifolds.
stance_target: whether isospectral hyperbolic triangle orbifolds exist in the literature
quoted_support: In this section, we exhibit isospectral but not isometric hyperbolic 2-orbifolds with volume 23π/6 and signature (0; 2^5, 3, 4).

claim: The isospectral pairs are proved via Vigneras' arithmetic (quaternion-algebra) method and are representation-equivalent (isospectral on all p-forms, not just functions), distinguished from isometry by the Chinburg-Friedman selectivity criterion, not by Sunada's method.
stance_target: construction mechanism for hyperbolic 2-orbifold isospectral pairs
quoted_support: By Theorem 2.20, the groups Γi are not selective, since B is ramified at p. We conclude using Theorem 2.17 that the hyperbolic 2-orbifolds X(Γ∗1) and X(Γ∗2) are isospectral but not isometric.

claim: A previously claimed isospectral pair of hyperbolic 2-orbifolds of genus 0 with signature (0;2,2,3,3) by Maclachlan-Rosenberger (1994) was later disproved by Buser-Flach-Semmler, who showed selectivity obstructs isospectrality -- a documented instance of a false isospectrality claim in this exact literature.
stance_target: reliability/history of claimed isospectral hyperbolic 2-orbifold examples
quoted_support: Finally, in 1994, Maclachlan and Rosenberger [61] claimed to have produced a pair of hyperbolic 2-orbifolds of genus 0 with orbifold fundamental groups of signature (0; 2, 2, 3, 3). However, Buser, Flach, and Semmler [14] later showed that these examples were too good to be true and that such orbifolds could not be Laplace isospectral.

claim: The example at signature (0;2,2,2,3,3), area 5*pi/3 (Example 4.20) is used as an illustration of a NEGATIVE case -- the paper proves this pair is NOT isospectral, using it to demonstrate the selectivity-verification technique.
stance_target: misreading signature (0;2,2,2,3,3) area 5pi/3 as a positive isospectral example
